column2: The ancestors are satisfied by offerings made here, increasing month by month: rhinoceros flesh, the great kalpa offering, honey, sages' food,
red-iron flesh, great vegetables, and the meat of a white-footed goat. One who gives these, and who is at Gaya, obtains everything as endless.
Likewise on the thirteenth day of the rainy season and especially under the Magha stars, he obtains a maiden, cattle and good sons,
gambling, farming and trade, two-hoofed and one-hoofed animals, sons with Vedic lustre, gold and silver and base metal,
chiefship among kinsmen and all desires; the giver of shraddha always obtains them. From the first day onward, excluding the fourteenth,
for those killed by weapon, it is given on that day. They give heaven, offspring, vigour, valour, land and strength,
sons and the best of them, good fortune, prosperity, eminence, auspiciousness, a prospering career, commerce and the like,
health, fame, freedom from grief, the highest goal, wealth, learning, a physician, success, base-metal limbs, and goats and sheep,
and horses and long life: one who gives shraddha by rule, from Krittika to Bharani, obtains his desires.
The believer, faithful, free of pride and envy: the ancestors — Vasus, Rudras and sons of Aditi — are the deities of shraddha.
Satisfied by shraddha, they gratify men's ancestors; they give long life, progeny, wealth, learning, heaven, liberation and happiness,
and, pleased, the ancestors give men kingship. Thus something has been told, especially in this chapter on rites (kalpa),
to be known in Vedic tradition and in other Puranas too. The wise man who reflects on this chapter on rites, O lord of sages,
becomes skilled in rites and gains an auspicious course here and elsewhere. The man who devoutly hears it in rites for gods and ancestors
gains the fruit of rites for gods and ancestors: wealth, learning, fame, sons, and the supreme goal hereafter.
After this I shall tell you briefly grammar, called the mouth of the Veda; listen attentively.
(Grammar: a list of words formed with various suffixes — malina, vikata, gomin, bhaurikividha, utkata, avatita, vanata, nibida, and similar forms.)
(Grammar: further derived words — nibirisa, meshukari, vitta, vidya, chana, vidyathu, bahutitha, parvata, shringin.)
(Grammar: svamin, vishamarupya, upatyaka, adhityaka, cilla, cipita, cikva, vatula, kutapa.)
(Grammar: valla, himelu, kahoda, upada, urnayu, marut, ekaki, charmanvati.)
(Grammar: jyotsna, tamisra, ashtivat, kakshivat, varshamanvati, asandivat, chakrivat, tushnika, jalpataki.)
(Grammar: the names Kambha, Kamyu, Kanva, Naradaketi, Kantu, Kantakampa, Shamva, Shanta, Shanti, Shamyashanta, Shamyuhamyu, Shubhamyuvat — word-forms with the suffix -yu and -va.)
Verb forms of "bhu" (to be): bhavati, babhuva, bhavita, bhavishyati, bhavatu, abhavat, bhavet.
Bhuyat, abhut, abhavishyat — these are the forms. Of "ad" (to eat): atti, jaghasa, attā, atsyati, attu, adat, adyat, ghasat, atsyat.
Of "hu" (to offer): juhoti, juhava, juhavanchakara, hota, hoshyati, juhotu, ajuhot, juhuyat, huyat, ahaushit, ahoshyat. Of "div": divyati, dideva, devita, devishyati, adivyat, divyet, divyat.
Adevit, adevishyat; of "su": sunoti, sushava, sota, soshyati, sunotu, asunot, sunuyat, suyat, asavit, asoshyat; and of "tud": tudati...
tutoda, totta, totsyati, tudatu, atudat, tudet, tudyat; atautsit, atotsyat; of "rudh": runaddhi, rurodha, roddha, rotsyati.
Runaddhu, arunat, rundhyat, arautsit, arotsyat; of "tan": tanoti, tatana, tanita, tanishyati, tanotu, atanot, tanuyat.

Atanit, atanit, atanishyat; of "kri": krinati, chikraya, kreta, kreshyati, krinatu, akrinat, krinat, krinniyat, kriyat, akraisit, akreshyat; of "chur": corayati, corayamasa, corayita, corayishyati, corayatu.
Acorayat, corayet, coryat, acucurat, acorishyat — thus ten classes (ganas) of roots. Causative: bhavayati; desiderative: bubhushati; intensive (repeated action): "bobhuyate", O sage.
Likewise with the elided intensive, "bobhavīti" is read. "Putriyati" (wishing for a son for oneself) and also in conduct, O Narada. For roots marked with anudatta or "n", for exchange of action,
and for roots beginning with "vish" and so on, O Brahmin, know the middle voice (atmanepada); the active voice (parasmaipada) is declared for the rest of agents by the grammarians.
Both voices for roots marked with "n" and svarita; and "ya" occurs in the passive and impersonal. To show the greatest ease, O sage,
the agent's action is not intended; in what is aimed at, others get agency: see "the rice cooks by itself".
A good knife cuts — so "the pot cooks", O sage. From a transitive root in the impersonal sense, and in the object, the "la" suffixes occur;
from an intransitive root, O Brahmin, in the impersonal and the agent. A root is intransitive when result and action rest in one;
transitive when they differ in the possessor. In a secondary object, with verbs like "druh", and in the principal object with "ni, hri, krish, vah";
of roots meaning knowledge or eating, and sound-verbs, at will; in the causative object, for others, the "la" endings of causative-ending roots are held to apply.
The finite endings are held to rest on the support of the root in result and action; in result the principal is the action; the ending's meaning is a qualifier.
Edhitavyam and "edhaniyam" are examples of the gerundive (krtya). Krtya endings are in the impersonal and object; krit endings are declared for the agent.
Karta and "karaka" and so on; in the past, the past forms are declared; the remainder is held in the aorist as indicated by "gamya" and the like.
In avyayibhava compounds like "adhistri" and "yathashakti"; in tatpurusha, "Ramashrita", "dhanyartha", "yupadaru".
Vyaghrabhi, "rajapurusha", "akshashaunda" — dvigu is declared: "panchagava", "dashagrami", "triphala" by usage.
Nilotpala, "mahashashthi" — karmadharaya in equal sense. "Abrahmana" is not given with "n"; potter and the like are formed by suffix.
In bahuvrihi with other meaning: "prapta-udaka grama", O Brahmin; "panchagu", "rupavadbharya", "madhyahna", "sasuta" and the like.
In collection (samuccaya): "serve the teacher and the lord"; in anvacaya: "bring alms, and a cow too" — in order for the two; this is the sentence for both.
In itaretara (mutual) compounds: "Rama and Krishna" are joined; "two and two", O Brahmin; "Brahman is worshipped as one".

(Astronomy: determining the longitude difference — placing the meridian line; the ‘rakshasa’ place, Mount Meru and the mountains, and the line through the middle: places on the line from Lanka to Ujjain and Meru.)
Ujjain (Avantika), Rohitaka, Sannihita lake, and the place of the weekday's change at the meridian — in terms of the 'half-loss' the correction increases.

By the difference in nadis of the other place, one prescribes subtraction for the west and addition for the east; the daily motion multiplied by the desired nadis and divided by sixty gives the minutes and so on.
This is to be subtracted for the past and added for the future: the planet of that moment. The zodiac circle is of 21,600 minutes; the maximum north-south latitude is eighty (parts).
Planets' latitude is deflected by their own node. For Mars (Kuja) it is twice the sine times three.
Mercury, Venus and the Sun are deflected by their nodes four-fold. One eighth of a sign's minutes is called the first half-chord (jyardha).
Then the one divided by two, less the quotient, mixed — that is the second. The first and the others in order, divided and reduced by the quotients,
are the twenty-four sine-differences (khandakas), the half-chord values in order. The maximum declination sine is 'seven-holes-gunas-moon' (i.e., 1397).
Multiplied by that, divided by the radius (trijya), the arc of that is the declination (kranti). Subtract the planet's apogee, and likewise subtract its "sighra" (fast) value,
the remainder is the arc of the 'kanda-pada'; from it the sine of the arc (bhujajya) and the cosine (koti) are had. For odd quadrants, from the past; the cosine from the future in the quadrant.
For the future, the sine of the arc and the cosine follow. The minutes divided by 225 (tattva-yama) give the quotient sine-sum already passed.
Multiplied by the difference between past and future, divide by 225; add the result obtained to the sine-sum named "past".
Likewise the rule for the ordinary sine applies to the reverse sine. The minutes divided by 225 give the sine-sum passed.
Multiplied by the difference between past and future, divide by 225; add the result to the sine-sum named "past".
And so is the reverse sine; subtract the sine; the remainder is to be divided to find the arc by the divisor.
The arc is the sum of the number-square (tattva-ashvi); the Sun's slow-epicycle parts are 14 and the Moon's are 13 (or so).
At the end of even and odd quadrants the minutes are reduced; of the two, at the end of the even: (the epicycle values for Mars and others are given).
For odd: 'two-mountains', 'well-disciplined', 'six-rudras-elephants-oceans' — thence for the fast epicycle of Mars and others at the even end: (numbers).
(Further numerical values of the epicycle radii for each planet in odd and even quadrants are listed.)
(Further numerical values for the fast epicycle, from the section on the fast correction.) The quantities multiplied by the odd-even difference are divided by the radius.
In the even circle, positive and negative are to be taken; the sine of the arc is increased or decreased; multiplied, the sine and cosine of the arc are divided by the number of planetary degrees.
The result of that arc's sine, the arc of the slow correction, is minutes and so on. The result of the fast cosine at the centre is positive from Capricorn onward.
In Cancer onward the cosine's result is to be subtracted from the radius. From the sum of the squares of the sine-results, the square-root is the fast-hypotenuse (karna).
The sine-result multiplied by the radius: positive from Capricorn, negative from Cancer onward by the cosine's result.
From the sum of the squares of those, the root is the hypotenuse called "chala". The sine-result multiplied by the radius, divided by the hypotenuse,
the arc of the quotient, minutes and so on, is the fast correction. This is first for Mars and others, and in the fourth operation.
One slow correction for Sun and Moon; for Mars and others: fast, slow, slow again, fast — four in order.
From the Aries start for all, in the slow and fast corrections; positive for planets in minutes; from Libra onward it is negative.
Multiplied by the sun's sine-result, divided by the planet's motion, in the minutes of the zodiac circle; the planet's minutes are done like the sun's.
The result is to be divided by the planet's; in the slow correction as for a planet; from Cancer positive, from Capricorn negative.
The motion multiplied by the sine of the arc and the next quantities, again divided by 225; multiplied by the slow epicycle, divided by degrees of the zodiac, they are minutes.
The motion corrected for the slow is from the fast and the apogee's motion; the remainder, with the difference, is to be multiplied by the radius, the number and the hypotenuse.
Divided by the circle's hypotenuse, when the hypotenuse exceeds the radius it is positive; negative when less; subtracting, the remainder gives the retrograde motion.
(Numerical thresholds for retrogression of Mars and the other planets: in degrees from the Sun.)
With the circle-purified degrees, retrogression arises. The sine of the ascension is multiplied by the equinoctial shadow; the terrestrial sine is divided by twelve.
Multiplied by the radius, divided by the day-diameter, is the arc; the enemies... The arc of that in the north declination is, with wealth lacking, separately lost.
One's own day-and-night quarter is half of the day or night; in southern declination reversed; doubled at the loss of day.
The lunar mansion's extent is 800 minutes; for the planet's minutes the mansion's extent gives the mansions; with motion and so on for the day.
Minutes of the sum of Sun and Moon divided by the extent of a yoga: the past and future multiplied by sixty give the nadis by the sum of motions.
Minutes of the Moon less the Sun's are divided by the extent to give tithis; past and future multiplied by sixty; divided by the motion.
The tithis from the bright first are doubled, one added, not stopped; the rest: Bava, Balava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara,
Vanij, then Vishti in the cloud; from the second half of the dark fortnight: Shakuni, Naga, Chatushpada, Kimstughna.
On a stone slab or on a plastered level, there with a gnomon of desired fingers he should draw a circle level to the ground.
In its middle he should set the gnomon, imagined as twelve fingers; where its shadow's tip touches the circle, in forenoon and afternoon,
there he should place a point in both circles named east and west; between them a line is drawn from south to north by a fish-figure.
Between the south and north directions the east-west line is drawn by a fish-figure; the intermediate directions are made likewise by the fish-figures.
He should draw a square outside by cords going out from the middle; the shadow-measure is taken by the arm-cords in fingers.
The line resting east-west is called the level circle; the circle of the stars is called the equinoctial circle.
The east-west line is to be determined; the amplitude lies between the desired shadow and the equinoctial shadow.
The root of the sum of the squares of the gnomon and shadow is the hypotenuse; subtracting the gnomon's square, the root is the shadow, and conversely.
The circle of the stars revolves eastward in thirty yugas (or "thirty times the yuga"); from the days elapsed, by the multiplication and division, what is got from the heap of days...
(Corrupted: rules for converting the mean planet to days and degrees, for shadow-correction.)
With the radius multiplied by the gnomon-shadow divided by the equinoctial (shadow), the sines of colatitude and latitude: for the shadow of the two, the colatitude and latitude are always south.
The sum of the sun's declination with latitude, with the difference of directions otherwise; the remaining parts of the sun's: its sine and cosine.
Multiplied by the gnomon measure in fingers, the sine of the arc and radius in order; divided by the cosine, the result is the shadow correction, outside the half-day.

Of the parts of one's own latitude and the sun's declination, when the directions agree, the difference; otherwise, the sum. The directional difference is the remaining declination; its sine times the radius,
divided by the maximum declination sine, the arc is the sun in the first quadrant; from Cancer onward subtract it from half the circle; from Libra add half the circle;
from Capricorn subtract it from the circle; the true sun at midday is obtained. Repeatedly applying its slow correction, the result of the mean sun's house.
The risings of the planets are the breaths multiplied; the motion divided by 'kha-kha-ashta-eka' (1800); the circle's breaths, with the result added, are the breaths of one's day-and-night.
Three signs from the sun... multiplied by half the hypotenuse, divided by half one's day-and-night; the sines in order, one, two, three; their arcs are separate.
Subtracting one's own below and below, from Aries the risings at Lanka are: (numbers) 1670, 1795, 1935 breaths.
Diminished by the terrestrial correction in one's own place, they are the desired risings; added with them in reverse order, Cancer and so on follow.
In reverse, the desired six, Libra and so on; the past and future breaths are to be made; the sun's tropical position desired.
Multiplied by one's own rising and divided, the future parts by one's measure; from the desired ghatika breaths he should subtract the future breaths.
Likewise the coming ascendant's breaths, and so in order the remainder is multiplied by thirty and divided by the unpurified.
With the degrees added or subtracted, the expense-degree is the body; Mars is... East-west, the desired nadis are multiplied, and the Lanka risings likewise.
Making the sun's loss and gain, the midheaven ascendant arises. The future breaths of the lesser, the past of the greater, are...
With sum and difference, the ascendant breaths; thus time is calculated. If Rahu and the sun's arc-degrees are small, the Moon's eclipse...
(Eclipse calculation: the sun and moon disk measures, the shadow of the earth covering the sun or moon, the amount covered.)
Half of the covered and covering measures less the latitude, excluding the part not eclipsed; and its own covered part, multiplied by ten...
multiplied by the covered amount, the root of it; the half-duration in ghatikas and so on is by the measures of fingers.
By desired palas, the less, added: (further steps to find the clear time of the eclipse's middle and end.)
With the eclipse magnitude multiplied by the portion; the covered measures are in vishopakas. The middle is at full moon's end; at new moon the...
Separately, the declination and latitude parts are corrected; the zenith distance parts arise. By that product, the square of the parts, less two...
(Parallax calculation: parallax in time and in latitude; the zenith distances.)
(Parallax continued — corrections of the lunar parallax, as for tithis.)
(Direction of the deflection (nati) and latitude of eclipse; direction by the zenith-distance parts.)
The latitude of those two, in one direction, becomes clear. Then the half-duration of the covering is to be found, with the half-durations...
By the parts of these with the parallaxes of the two, as before; corrected by them, the half-duration is clear.
Less and added with those, the middle of the new moon, the times at the ends. The sun and the rest... (eclipse contact times).
With the sun diminished and increased by those times of the parts, the moon's setting and rising occur. Having first seen the planet's disk, the observed...
(Observation of eclipse phases at rising and setting — the parts covered are to be known by the wise as past or future tithis.)
In reverse, with the parts of conjunction and doubled tithi-division clearly; the corrected parallax is had in fingers and so on.
(The moon's horn and the direction of its tip are drawn according to the angular measure; the 'valana' (deflection) drawing in fingers.)
(Planetary conjunctions: the remainder multiplied by the hypotenuse, separately — the figures of planets, to be reduced.)
When the hypotenuse exceeds the radius... the bodies are divided from Mars. The difference of straight and retrograde, divided by the difference in motions...
The sum of the motions of retrograde and direct planets, in days to come or past; the latitude... the sum or difference when the north and south are alike.
The difference between a north planet and a south planet; when it is less than the sum of the disks; the parallax and so on to be made clear as at a solar eclipse.
When the sun and moon are on one path (ayana), if their declinations are equal in the combined circle, it is called Dhrita (Vaidhriti).
When they are on opposite paths, with the moon's form and the declination-minutes equal, that is Vyatipata. In half the zodiac circle, joined with the sun...
When the sun and moon stand at the end of the star-circle and the half-circle, their declinations calculated as seen, joined with the parts...
Then, for the moon going in an odd quadrant, the declination corrected for the latitude: if the sun's declination is greater, the Pata is past.
If less, it is to come; and left for the even quadrant. When the moon's declination differs from the latitude and gets purified,
the two declination arcs, with radius and maximum declination multiplied, their arc... for the going and the coming.
The Pata is subtracted from the moon... and multiplied by the Sun's motion; divided by the Moon's motion, the Sun's result in minutes is like the Moon.
The result of the Moon's Pata should be given reversed. This work is repeated until the declinations are equal.
When the declinations are equal, that is the Pata; when the added parts are less than the Moon's, the time in ghatikas of half night is to come, the greater is present.
The two half-circles being fixed, the difference of the minutes divided by sixty and by the Moon's motion gives the nadis of the time of Pata.
Half the sum of the Sun's and Moon's disks multiplied by sixty is divided by the difference of the motions; the result is the half-duration in nadis and so on.
The true middle of the Pata, less the half-duration, is its time of occurrence; its conjunction is called the beginning.
Between the beginning and end times the time is to be known as most terrible, blazing like fire, condemned for all rites.
Thus this has been told in outline, O Brahmin, about calculation; I shall now speak, at the proper time, of birth-horoscopy, beginning with the names of signs.
She is of seen form and nature; of those two in odd signs it is held so. Then the malefic, lacking qualities, when those two are aspected by malefics.
